report_name: New 'Wazza' Phishkit Uses Advanced Evasion to Target Global Orgs

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The Wazza campaign uses a link in a phishing email as the initial access vector to direct victims into a multi-stage routing chain.

attack_patterns.name: Execution Guardrails
attack_patterns.description: The Wazza phishkit uses a multi-stage routing chain to perform checks on visitors, filtering out security scanners, sandboxes, VPNs, and datacenter IPs to ensure the payload is only delivered to human targets.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The campaign uses Device Code phishing to trick users into authorizing a malicious application, allowing the attacker to steal authentication tokens to bypass MFA.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The Wazza campaign uses an Adobe-themed Device Code phishing page to trick the user into authorizing a malicious application to access their account.

malware.name: Wazza
malware.description: A sophisticated phishing kit that uses a multi-stage routing chain to filter out automated analysis systems and deliver a final phishing page to human victims. It targets banking, manufacturing, and government sectors.

identities.name: Adobe
identities.description: The Wazza phishkit uses Adobe-themed lures and phishing pages to impersonate the company and trick victims.

infrastructure.name: Wazza Routing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: A multi-stage chain of domains and endpoints used to filter out automated traffic and route legitimate victims to the final phishing page.

infrastructure.name: Wazza Adobe Phishing Page
infrastructure.description: The final payload of the campaign, an Adobe-themed Device Code phishing page designed to steal authentication tokens.

indicators.name: Suspicious Adobe-themed Phishing URL
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Adobe-themed Phishing URL
id: 7c5b1a8e-3f0d-4b9a-8c1d-6e2f4a0b9c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects potential phishing URLs that contain 'adobe' or 'document' but do not originate from legitimate Adobe domains. This pattern is associated with the Wazza phishkit.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/wazza-phishkit-targets-banking.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains:
      - 'adobe'
      - 'document'
  filter:
    cs-host|endswith:
      - '.adobe.com'
      - '.behance.net'
      - '.adobelogin.com'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects potential phishing URLs that contain 'adobe' or 'document' but do not originate from legitimate Adobe domains, a technique used by the Wazza phishkit.
